topics.label: Introduction to the Complement Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture with welcoming remarks and an introductory analogy highlighting the importance and complexity of the complement system.

topics.label: Core Concepts and Fundamentals of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture of the complement cascade, its naming conventions, and the central biochemical role of C3.

topics.label: Complement Activation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three recognition pathways—alternative, lectin, and classical—that initiate the complement cascade and converge on C3 convertase formation.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Activated Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary effector outcomes of complement activation, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane attack complex lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation and Self-Protection Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical Presentations of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic and acquired deficiencies in specific complement components produce distinct clinical diseases and susceptibility patterns.

topics.label: Pathogen Strategies for Complement Evasion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the evolutionary mechanisms used by pathogens to subvert complement defenses, focusing on the specific adaptations of Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the session with concluding remarks and previews the subject of the upcoming lecture.
